You absolutely CAN refuse to use these and the practice are legally bound to accept appointment bookings via telephone and all other correspondence carried out by letter.
The Human rights act 1998 articles 8 & 14, the Equality act 2010 including the public sector equality duty s149 and NHS England's own policies mean that mandatory use of any app or digital means of accessing health care may discriminate against patients who are digitally excluded, including those with disabilities, low literacy, limited internet access or limited technical ability.
Furthermore should you enforce your right to go non digital with this practice you can then proceed to request all data packets historically transmitted, stored or otherwise by the digital platform used, use an FOI for this.
In summary, if you're having difficulties using the apps that they claim are compulsory contact reception today and make them aware of your rights.
Of course, that's if they don't hang up on you.
